paragraphs: Here's what jumps out at me, friend. Nehemiah is scared. The text says he was "overwhelmed with fear" (Nehemiah 2:2). And he still tells the king the truth about his broken heart. Hiding it would have been safer, and he didn't pick safer. I think that's a man who knew whose face he was really standing in front of.

Now look at the moment the king says, "What is your request?" Nehemiah doesn't ask for a night to think it over. The very next words are, "So I prayed to the God of heaven" (Nehemiah 2:4). That prayer is quick, right in the middle of the conversation, and I love it. You can pray in the middle of the hard moment too, with no special room and no fancy words. God is already listening.

And then the yes comes, and Nehemiah tells us why: "the gracious hand of my God was upon me" (Nehemiah 2:8). He asked for a lot, and he gives God the credit for every bit of it. But the very last verse shows opposition already showing up, because good work doesn't always get applause (Nehemiah 2:10). So here's the big idea: bring your burden to God, pray in the moment, and give Him the thanks. The story isn't over, friend, so keep your oven warm.
